# Instant updates

Vault Secrets Operator (VSO) can instantly update corresponding Kubernetes Secrets when
changes are made in Vault, by subscribing to [Vault Events][vault-events] via a
persistent WebSocket connection. Setting a periodic refresh interval is still
recommended since event message delivery is not guaranteed.

<Note title="Requires Vault Enterprise 1.16.3+">

Instant updates require [Vault Enterprise](/vault/docs/enterprise) 1.16.3+ due
to the use of [Vault Event Notifications][vault-events].

</Note>

Choose the guide for your secret type:

- [KV v1 / v2 static secrets (VaultStaticSecret)](#kv-static-secrets)
- [Auto-rotated static credentials — database / LDAP (VaultDynamicSecret)](#auto-rotated-static-credentials)
- [Dynamic lease-based credentials (VaultDynamicSecret)](#dynamic-lease-based-credentials)

---

## KV static secrets

Enable instant updates for [VaultStaticSecret][vss-spec] resources backed by a
KV v1 or KV v2 secrets engine. Vault fires a `kv` event on every write to the
secret path and VSO reconciles immediately, using the `X-Vault-Index` header to
avoid stale reads on Vault Performance Standbys.

### Before you start

- **You must have [Vault Secrets Operator](/vault/docs/platform/k8s/vso/sources/vault) installed**.
- **You must use [Vault Enterprise](/vault/docs/enterprise) version 1.16.3 or later**.

### Step 1: Set event permissions (KV)

Grant these permissions in the policy associated with the VaultAuth role:

```hcl
path "<kv mount>/<kv secret path>" {
  capabilities = ["read", "list", "subscribe"]
  subscribe_event_types = ["*"]
}

path "sys/events/subscribe/kv*" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}
```

<Tip>

See [Event Notifications Policies][events-policies] for more information on
Vault event notification permissions.

</Tip>

### Step 2: Enable instant updates on the VaultStaticSecret

Set `syncConfig.instantUpdates: true` in the [VaultStaticSecret spec][vss-spec]:

```yaml
---
apiVersion: secrets.hashicorp.com/v1beta1
kind: VaultStaticSecret
metadata:
  namespace: vso-example
  name: vault-static-secret-v2
spec:
  vaultAuthRef: vault-auth
  mount: <kv mount>
  type: kv-v2
  path: <kv secret path>
  version: 2
  refreshAfter: 1h
  destination:
    create: true
    name: static-secret2
  syncConfig:
    instantUpdates: true
```

## Auto-rotated static credentials

Enable instant updates for [VaultDynamicSecret][vds-spec] resources that sync
credentials Vault rotates on a schedule, such as database or LDAP static roles.
When a rotation event fires, VSO reads the fresh credentials immediately using
the `X-Vault-Index` header to avoid stale reads on Vault Performance Standbys.

VSO subscribes to a single engine WebSocket (resolved from `sys/mounts/<mount>`,
e.g. `database`, `ldap`, or any other engine that emits rotation events). No
lease WebSocket is needed because the rotation event itself is the trigger.

### Before you start

- **You must have [Vault Secrets Operator](/vault/docs/platform/k8s/vso/sources/vault) installed**.
- **You must use [Vault Enterprise](/vault/docs/enterprise) version 1.16.3 or later**.
- **The VaultAuth policy must grant `read` on `sys/mounts/*`** so VSO can
  resolve the engine type at runtime.

### Step 1: Set event permissions (database / LDAP / Azure static roles)

Grant these permissions in the policy associated with the VaultAuth role:

**Database static roles:**

```hcl
# Allow VSO to resolve the mount's engine type
path "sys/mounts/*" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}

# Allow VSO to read credentials and subscribe to rotation events
path "database/*" {
  capabilities = ["read", "list", "subscribe"]
  subscribe_event_types = ["*"]
}

# Allow subscribing to database engine events
path "sys/events/subscribe/database*" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}
```

**LDAP static roles:**

```hcl
# Allow VSO to resolve the mount's engine type
path "sys/mounts/*" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}

# Allow VSO to read credentials and subscribe to rotation events
path "ldap/*" {
  capabilities = ["read", "subscribe"]
  subscribe_event_types = ["*"]
}

# Allow subscribing to LDAP engine events
path "sys/events/subscribe/ldap*" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}
```

**Azure static roles:**

```hcl
# Allow VSO to resolve the mount's engine type
path "sys/mounts/*" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}

# Allow VSO to read static credentials and role definitions
path "azure/static-creds/*" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}

path "azure/static-roles/*" {
  capabilities = ["read", "list", "subscribe"]
  subscribe_event_types = ["*"]
}

# Allow subscribing to Azure engine events
path "sys/events/subscribe/azure*" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}
```

### Step 2: Enable instant updates on the VaultDynamicSecret

Set `spec.allowStaticCreds: true` and `syncConfig.instantUpdates: true` in the
[VaultDynamicSecret spec][vds-spec]:

```yaml
---
apiVersion: secrets.hashicorp.com/v1beta1
kind: VaultDynamicSecret
metadata:
  namespace: vso-example
  name: vault-dynamic-secret-db-static
spec:
  vaultAuthRef: vault-auth
  mount: database
  path: static-creds/my-static-role
  allowStaticCreds: true
  refreshAfter: 1h
  destination:
    create: true
    name: db-static-secret
  syncConfig:
    instantUpdates: true
```

## Dynamic lease-based credentials

Enable instant updates for [VaultDynamicSecret][vds-spec] resources that issue
new credentials on request (dynamic leases). VSO subscribes to two WebSockets:
one for the engine type (e.g. `database`) and one for `lease` events so that
credential revocations and expirations trigger an immediate re-issuance, using
the `X-Vault-Index` header to avoid stale reads on Vault Performance Standbys.

### Before you start

- **You must have [Vault Secrets Operator](/vault/docs/platform/k8s/vso/sources/vault) installed**.
- **You must use [Vault Enterprise](/vault/docs/enterprise) version 1.16.3 or later**.
- **The VaultAuth policy must grant `read` on `sys/mounts/*`** so VSO can
  resolve the engine type at runtime.

### Step 1: Set event permissions (dynamic leases)

Grant these permissions in the policy associated with the VaultAuth role:

**Database dynamic credentials:**

```hcl
# Allow VSO to resolve the mount's engine type
path "sys/mounts/*" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}

# Allow VSO to read and subscribe to credential events
path "database/*" {
  capabilities = ["read", "list", "subscribe"]
  subscribe_event_types = ["*"]
}

# Allow subscribing to database engine events
path "sys/events/subscribe/database*" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}

# Allow subscribing to lease lifecycle events (revoke / expire)
path "sys/events/subscribe/lease*" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}
```

For other engines, replace the `database/*` paths with the equivalent paths for
your engine:

| Engine | Paths to substitute |
|---|---|
| LDAP | `ldap/*` |
| Azure | `azure/creds/*`, `azure/roles/*` |
| AWS | `aws/creds/*`, `aws/roles/*` |

### Step 2: Enable instant updates on the VaultDynamicSecret

Set `syncConfig.instantUpdates: true` in the [VaultDynamicSecret spec][vds-spec].
Do **not** set `allowStaticCreds: true` for dynamic lease credentials:

```yaml
---
apiVersion: secrets.hashicorp.com/v1beta1
kind: VaultDynamicSecret
metadata:
  namespace: vso-example
  name: vault-dynamic-secret-db
spec:
  vaultAuthRef: vault-auth
  mount: database
  path: creds/my-postgresql-role
  destination:
    create: true
    name: dynamic-db-secret
  syncConfig:
    instantUpdates: true
```

---

## Debugging

Check Kubernetes events on the resource to see if VSO subscribed to Vault event
notifications successfully.

### Example: VSO is subscribed to Vault event notifications

```shell-session
$ kubectl describe vaultstaticsecret vault-static-secret-v2 -n vso-example
...
Events:
  Type    Reason               Age              From               Message
  ----    ------               ----             ----               -------
  Normal  SecretSynced         2s               VaultStaticSecret  Secret synced
  Normal  EventWatcherStarted  2s (x2 over 2s)  VaultStaticSecret  Started watching events
  Normal  SecretRotated        2s               VaultStaticSecret  Secret synced
```

For a `VaultDynamicSecret` with `instantUpdates: true`, the event message
includes the engine type resolved at runtime:

```shell-session
$ kubectl describe vaultdynamicsecret vault-dynamic-secret-db -n vso-example
...
Events:
  Type    Reason              Age   From                Message
  ----    ------              ----  ----                -------
  Normal  SecretSynced        5s    VaultDynamicSecret  Secret synced
  Normal  EventWatcherStarted 5s    VaultDynamicSecret  Started watching database events
```

### Example: The VaultAuth role policy lacks the required event permissions

```shell-session
$ kubectl describe vaultstaticsecret vault-static-secret-v2 -n vso-example
...
Events:
  Type     Reason             Age   From               Message
  ----     ------             ----  ----               -------
  Normal   SecretSynced       2s    VaultStaticSecret  Secret synced
  Warning  EventWatcherError  2s    VaultStaticSecret  Error while watching events:
   failed to connect to vault websocket: error returned when opening event stream
   web socket to wss://vault.vault.svc.cluster.local:8200/v1/sys/events/subscribe/kv%2A?json=true,
   ensure VaultAuth role has correct permissions and Vault is Enterprise version
   1.16 or above: {"errors":["1 error occurred:\n\t* permission denied\n\n"]}
  Normal   SecretRotated      2s    VaultStaticSecret  Secret synced
```

### Example: VSO cannot resolve the mount type for a VaultDynamicSecret

If the VaultAuth policy is missing `sys/mounts/*` read permission, VSO emits:

```shell-session
$ kubectl describe vaultdynamicsecret vault-dynamic-secret-db -n vso-example
...
Events:
  Type     Reason             Age   From                Message
  ----     ------             ----  ----                -------
  Warning  EventWatcherError  2s    VaultDynamicSecret  Cannot determine Vault mount type
   for "database": permission denied. Ensure the VaultAuth policy grants read on
   sys/mounts/*. Engine-event subscription skipped; will retry next reconcile.
```

Add `path "sys/mounts/*" { capabilities = ["read"] }` to the VaultAuth policy
to resolve this.
